Below is an example of how to write a Haskell program that reads the contents of another Python script (`python.py`) as input, interpolates a given list of strings (in this case `["code"]`), and then prints out the modified output.

```haskell
{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}

import Control.Monad (replicateM_)
main = do
    putStrLn "Please enter the path to your python interpreter"
    interpreterPath <- getLine
    print $ concat. map (\x -> x ++ "\n") $ evalStateT runPythonInterpreter interpreterPath ["['code']"]

runPythonInterpreter :: String -> [String] -> StateT String IO ()
runPythonInterpreter _ []     = pure []
runPythonInterpreter interpreterPath ["print('\"code\")"]   = do
        let filePath = interpreterPath++"/python.exe"
            command  = "python \"" ++ filePath ++ "\" << EOF\n\n"

        putStr $ intercalate "" $
                    takeWhile (/='\n')
                      $ lines <$> readFile (interpreterPath ++ "/setup.cfg")
        
        replicateM_ 10 $ do
            let command' = command ++ "'\"'" ++ unwords ['<', take 1 ("\"[" : tail args), '>', '\n']
            lift $ system command'
            
        return []
```
